Introduction
This method is used to determine the dielectric strength of insulating liquids using the Russian Kinitron apparatus, which complies with the Russian specifications TOCT 6919-54. One of the most important factors for the success of this test is strict adherence to the operating steps of the apparatus and the Russian methods.
This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, tested by the technical supervisor Awad Toghan Mohamed, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Measuring the dielectric strength of insulating liquids gives an important indication of the extent of oil contamination with moisture or impurities, even in small quantities, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material.
Measurement Theory
The voltage is raised on the oil sample at a uniform rate until breakdown occurs in the oil; the reading is recorded each time, then the average of the readings is taken, and the resulting breakdown voltage (in kilovolts) is the voltage the oil can withstand.
Definition
It is the maximum voltage (kV) the oil can withstand as an insulating material when tested. | Dielectric strength (breakdown voltage)
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 
When the apparatus is not in use, the cell and electrode are stored with usable oil in them, placed in their place in the apparatus, away from dust and dirt. | 
Personal Safety Procedures
Stand on a pedal made of insulating material that is dry, clean and not punctured. | 1.
Wear insulating gloves when working on the apparatus, and make sure they are fit for use through their previous tests. | 2.
Do not touch the apparatus during measurement, and place your other hand behind your back; this is safer. | 3.
Environmental Recommendations
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 1.
Tools and Equipment Used
The Russian Kinitron apparatus, whose range reaches 70 kV. | 1.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Remove the test cell from inside the apparatus and empty the oil inside it; make sure the distance between the two electrode poles is 2.5 mm, using the gauge provided for that purpose. | 1.
Invert the sample bottle to be tested gently several times until the oil sample is homogeneous, without causing any air bubbles to form. | 2.
Wash the test cell with the oil to be tested more than once to ensure the cell is clean of any impurities or sediment. | 
Fill the test cell with the sample to be tested slowly to avoid bubbles forming, and fill it up to the mark. | 4.
Dry the test cell from the outside, then place it in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door. | 5.
Place the test cell in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door. | 5.
Stand on the insulating pedal, make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus, then connect it to the electric power source and press the power switch. | 6.
Start raising the voltage manually using the lever, at a raising rate of (1 kV/s), until the sound indicating oil breakdown is heard; then record the voltage at which the oil breakdown occurred. | 7.
Repeat the previous step five times, with a time interval of 5 minutes between raisings, taking care to stir and clean with a special glass rod between the electrodes each time; record the reading each time, then take the average of the last five readings, which is the voltage the oil can withstand. | 8.
